Plain Weave Fabrics: Derivatives of plain weave and their characteristic. Ornamentation of plain woven fabrics by varying set, yarn linear density, crimp, twist and others material. Twill weaves: Definition of the terms balanced, warp-faced and weft-faced twill weaves, developed twill weaves, waved, herringbone, diamond and elongated, relative firmness of twill weaves, large twills influence of the twist of the yarns, angle of inclination of twill weaves. Satin and sateen weave: Introduction, formula number, design. Fancy designs of fabrics: Characteristic, appearance and texture of simple fancy weaves (viz, mock leno including distorted thread effects), huckaback honeycomb, basic crepe weaves and bedford cord structures; Stripe and check effects using basic and simple fancy weaves. Figuring with Extra Thread: Designs of fabrics figured with extra weft and extra warp; Compound fabrics, Stitched double cloth. Color and Weave Effect: Color in combination with weave effects, i.e. pinstripe, crowfoot, dog's tooth, shepherds check.

Knitted Fabric Structure: Structure of 1x1 rib and 1x1 purl weft knitted fabrics and their representation on design paper; Comparison of the properties of plain, 1x1 purl weft knitted fabrics. Structures of simple, tuck and miss stitches and their representation using loop diagrams; Representation using conventional notation: 1x1 straight lock, 1x1 cross lock, half-cardigan, full-cardigan, 1x1 weft locknit and 2x1 weft locknit structures.

TE 3110.title: Sessional on TE 3109
topics: Sessional based on TE 3109.

IPE 3221.title: Industrial Management
topics: Management Fundamentals: Introduction to Management Concept, nature of management and purpose, development of management theories and principles of management, modern management thoughts; Management by Objectives (MBO); Forecasting; Decision making, decision making tools, steps of decision making; Basic concept of Management Information System (MIS); Organizing- Types of organizations; Organizational structure; Span of control; Authority; Centralization and decentralization of administration; Chain of command.
Business: Common features of business enterprises, Single ownership, partnership, Joint Stock Company, cooperative society, public sector, private sector.

Human Resource Management: Manpower planning; Recruitment and Training; Theories of motivation; Job evaluation; Merit rating; Leadership style and types; Morale and its importance; Salary and wages, wage incentive plans; Job rotation.
Management Tools: Total Quality Management (TQM); TPM; Quality circles; 5S principles; Kaizen concepts; Lean manufacturing.
Industrial and Research Association: Brief profile and role of Association of Industries, ISO series.

Shedding: Tappet shedding; Construction of shedding Tappet. Dobby Shedding: Scope and classification, negative, positive and cross-border, peg-plan, timing and dwell of dobby. Jacquard Shedding: Scope, types and basic principle of jacquard shedding. Picking: Classification; Over picking and under picking mechanisms, Construction of picking tappet, picking faults. Beating: Principle of crank and crank arm beating; Effect of crank arm and crank length, Sley eccentricity and its effects, Forces involved in beating action. Take-up and Let-off Mechanisms: Calculation of take-up constant; Picks/cm and rate of let off Automation in weaving; Production of various stripe and check fabrics; necessary calculations.

Knitting: Stitches produced by varying the timing of the needles, loop intermeshing. Derivatives of single jersey and double jersey structures. Knitted fabric faults and their remedies. Hosiery Machines: Hosiery machine drive; Control mechanism and sequence; Hosiery yarns; Mechanism for welts, heel and toe production, Hosiery stitch control mechanism. Flat Bed Knitting Machine: Parameters, operations, knitting action and cam arrangement. Straight Bar Frame - Development; Fully fashioned article; knitting action of straight bar frame, rib to plain machines; Relevant calculations. Warp Knitting: Introduction, Classification, Basic principles; Study on Tricot and Raschel machine and their knitting action; Crochet machine and it's knitting action; Tricot two full set guide bar machine and its products and structure and design; Basic calculations.

TE 3204.title: Sessional on TE 3203
topics: Sessional based on TE 3203.

TE 3205.title: Wet Processing Engineering-II
topics: Dyeing: Reactive Dyes: Structure and properties; Classification of reactive dyes; Reaction mechanism of reactive dyes with cellulose; Basic principles of dyeing with reactive dyes; Application methods of reactive dyes; Disadvantages, after treatment, fastness properties; Recent development in reactive dyeing; Faults and remedies. Disperse Dyes: Discovery and development; Properties and chemical structure; Classification; Fabric preparation for polyester fabric; Mechanism of dispersing action; Carrier, Application methods, after treatment; Fastness properties; Concept of rapid dyeing; Faults and remedies. Sulpher Dyes: History and development; Synthesis; Structure and properties; Classification of sulpher; Forms of sulpher dye; Vatting of sulpher dyes; Dyeing mechanism, application methods; Fastness properties; Risk for environment with sulpher dyes and the approach to solve the problems; Faults and remedies. Azoic Colors: General properties; Dyeing mechanism; Different naphthols and bases, Application methods; After-treatment; Role of bath additives; faults and remedies.

Printing: Reactive Printing: Fabric preparation; Thickener; Print paste preparation; All in one method with suitable recipe; Two stage method; Washing off reactive prints; Effect of chemical finishing. Printing with Disperse Dyes: Fabric preparation; Dye selection; Print paste formulation; Thickener; Fixation; After treatment. Printing with Sulpher Dyes: Fabric preparation; Dye selection; Thickener; All in one method; Two stage methods; Function of different ingredients; After treatment. Printing with Insoluble Azoic Colors: Fabric preparation; Base printing; Naphtholate printing; Rapid fast and rapidogen colors; Aftertreatment. Pigment Printing: Structure of pigment; Garment printing; Novelty printing effects; Economics of printing process.

Finishing: Introduction; Physical and mechanical finishing of cotton, jute and wool fabrics; Physical and chemical softening processes, selection of chemical and evaluation of softening; Detailed study on calendaring, raising, sanforizing, anti-crease finish on cotton, water repellent finishes on cotton, in finishing, mercerization, parchmentisation and flame retardant finish; Special finishing treatments: Rot-proofing, mildew proofing, insect and antimicrobial finishes, soil lease, anti-state finishes.

TE 3206.title: Sessional on TE 3205
topics: Sessional based on TE 3205.

Alternative Methods of Fabric Joining: Objects; Limitations; Methods: Welding, adhesive, fusing, moulding and their comparison.

Trimmings and Accessories: Label; Motif; Fabrics for support and insulation: Linings, interlinings, wadding, shoulder pads; Narrow fabric trims: Lace, braid, elastic, seam binding and tape; Fastenings: Hook and loop fastening, zip fasteners, buttons, eyelets and laces; International care labeling code; Performance of trimmings.
Pressing and Finishing: Objects; Types; Equipment and methods; Control of the pressing process; Non-iron garments; Folding, packing; Quality control in finishing; Inspection, brief discussion on AQL.

TE 3208.title: Sessional on TE 3207

TE 3231.title: Merchandising and Marketing
topics: Textile Merchandising: Introduction to merchandising- the activities involved; Role of merchandiser, qualities of a merchandiser, responsibility of the merchandiser; Visual merchandising and its advantages for the buyer and seller today; Fashion calendar, the planning cycle, merchandise planner; Trend prediction: forecasting, trend/ color forecasting, sales forecasting; Product selection and mix, distribution mix, distribution channels from producer to ultimate consumer; Supply chains: store retailing, non-store retailing; Buying calendar; Buying strategy; Customer identification; Supplier- retailer relationship; Sourcing & global sourcing; Range planning and range building.

Textile Marketing: Marketing: Definition and core concepts; The specificity of marketing for the textile and apparel market; Production concept, product concept, selling concept, marketing and societal marketing concept; Marketing strategies and the marketing mix for the textile and apparel market; Product: Levels of product, product hierarchy, stages in new product development, product life cycle and its stages, product mix, product line; Price: Factors to consider when setting price, pricing strategies; Channels of distribution; Promotion Mix: Advertising, sales promotion, personal selling and public relations, factors in setting the promotion mix with supporting examples from textile industry; Marketing information system; The essence of market segmentation: consumer and industrial market; Consumers' behavior, factors affecting CB, buyer's decision process and type of behavior; Corporate social responsibility and its importance to marketing of textile and clothing companies.

Comfort: Measurement of air, water permeability/ retention.
Fastness Test: Factors and types of fastness; Measurement of fastness to light, washing and rubbing; Estimation of damage to materials caused by physical and chemical treatments, chlorine bleach.
Water Repellency: Wet ability of fabrics, spray rating test, hydrostatic head test.
Serviceability: Serviceability; Wear and abrasion tests; Piling of fabrics; Snagging; Crease recovery.
Carpet Testing: Testing related to carpet thickness, compression and durability.
Flammability Testing: Definitions, factors, available test methods, recent developments in flammability testing.
Testing related to Textile Wet Processing: Water testing; Methods of estimating available chlorine; Test for mercerization; Tests for determining types of size in the fabric.
Regulatory Organization: Oeko-Tex, REACH, GOTS, ECHA, WRAP, their legislation, certification process etc.

TE 4114.title: Sessional on TE 4113
topics: Sessional based on TE 4113.

Carbon Fiber: Manufacture of PAN-based, Pitch-based carbon fibers, physical properties and applications; carbon nanotubes and applications
Glass Fiber: Fiber manufacture; fiber properties; glass-fiber composites and other applications
Ceramic and other High Performance Fibers: Manufacture of ceramic fibers, production of chemically resistant fibers and thermally resistant fibers, Basalt Fiber.
Specialty Fibers: Hollow and profile fibers; blended and bi-component fibers, super absorbent fibers; film Fibers.

Major components of fiber reinforced composite materials: matrix, reinforcement, fillers and other additives, types of composites, matrices and reinforcement. Textile structure for composites, unidirectional, planar, 3D, net-shaped, woven, knitted, braided and nonwoven. The fiber-matrix interface; role of coupling agents. Composite manufacturing process, thermoset and thermoplastics. Testing of composite materials (mechanical). Mechanics of composite materials. Nanocomposites: introduction, process and applications.

Fabrics for architectural and constructions, awnings and canopies, roofing material, storage vessels; Fiber reinforced concrete and cement; Acoustic and heat insulation textiles.
Medical Textiles: Definition, raw materials; classifications, fiber architecture and fabric constructions for different application in medical textiles, healthcare and hygiene textiles.
Protective Clothing: Brief idea about different type of protective clothing; Functional requirement of textiles in protective clothing, description of different protective clothing, parachute cloth.
Coated and Laminated Textiles: Coating, types, polymeric materials and fabric substrates for coating, methods of coating, micro porous coating, hydrophilic coating.
Sports and Recreation Textiles: Functional requirement of different type of product and their construction; Sports uniforms; Sports equipment; Skates; Bikes; Marine products.
Automotive Textiles: Application of textiles in automobiles; Requirement and design for different tyre, airbags and belts; Methods of production and properties of textiles used in these applications.
Smart Textiles: Introduction, types, materials used applications. Application of phase change material in smart textiles, brief discussion of smart shirt, smart suit and musical jacket.

Air Pollution: Sources and types of pollutants; Effects of various pollutants on human health; Materials and plants; Air pollution meteorology; Global warming; Air pollution monitoring and control measures. Noise Pollution: General consideration; Industrial noise sources evaluation; Methods and techniques to control and reduce noise level.

Chemical Used in Textile Industry: Toxicity of various chemicals, viz alkalis, oxidizing and reducing agents, acids, carriers, resins and bleaching agents etc. Role of each chemical on waste water load.

Textile Effluents: Effluents and their characterization; Methods of effluent treatment, disposal of effluents, study of Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) in textile processing; Effects of textile waste in environment pollution.

Waste Management: Composition of wastes, collection systems and alternatives for treatments and re-use, reduction of textile waste water using automatic process control; Recycle, filtration and waste water analysis; Determination for waste treatment costing.

IPE 4223.title: Operations Management
topics: Introduction: Historical evolution of production and operations Management; Strategic role of operations, trends in operations management, process and control of operations strategies.

Work Study: Definition, objectives, techniques, purpose of work study, steps and different phases. Method Study: Definition, steps, selection of problems, collection of facts and consideration about objectives, recording techniques, elements of a process analysis, various types of associated chart. Motion Study: Operation analysis, motion analysis, motion economy, two handed process chart, micro motion study; Therbligs; Simo chart; Examples from Textile and Apparel industries. Work Measurement: Definition, uses, techniques; Time Study, measuring instruments and elements in time study, factors, alignment chart, performance rating methods, observed time and normal time, allowances, standard time; Work sampling; Predetermined motion time study, Motion time data for assembly operations; Work factor system, method of time measurement.

Inventory Management: Inventory concepts, classification, inventory models.
Line Balancing: Objectives, procedure, techniques, applications in Textile and Apparel industries.

Operation Scheduling: Introduction, flow shop and job shop scheduling, project scheduling with CPM and PERT.
Operations Research: Introduction to optimization, linear programming, distribution methods, assignment models, decision analysis, queuing theory and game theory.

Lubricants, properties, lubrication in textile equipments; Seals, leakage from textile equipments and its prevention. Wear and tear in bearing and other moving parts of textile equipments, Bearing and repair of bearing of textile equipments.
Materials Handling: Conveyors used in textile mill, belt conveyor, chain conveyer, hydraulic press and lift, truck hoist.
Ergonomics: Definition; Importance and application of ergonomics of work place and layout.

Safety Management: Concepts and techniques; Accident investigation and reporting; Safety performance monitoring; Safety education and training. Safety in Textile Mill: Physical, chemical, biological and ergonomic hazards of textile industry and their prevention; Industrial toxicology; Safety devices; Safety rules; Factory act about safety; Safety culture; First aid.

Eco Fibers: Focused on natural fibers, man-made fibers, innovations linked with eco-friendly fibers, biodegradable and sustainable fibers.
Organic Cotton: necessity, production practices, Post-harvest handling/processing, limitation, obligatory standards for organic cotton and organic cotton certifiers.
Environmental Aspects of Textile Dyeing and Finishing: General considerations and problems regarding dyes, dyeing, eco-finishing and their impact on environment.

Green Textiles: Enzyme biotechnology; Plasma technology for textiles; Role of UV and Gamma radiation on textiles; Bio-degradation studies of textile and clothing products; Renewable textiles; eco-labeling for textiles and apparels.
Tools in Assessing the Sustainability: Sustainable Textile Production (STeP); The Higg Index; The sustainable apparel index; Standards and test methods for sustainability.

Testing: Standards and methods of testing nonwoven fabrics.

Nanofibers: Genesis, history and terminology. Methods of producing nanofibers. Electrospinning of nanofibers. Influence of different parameters on electrospinning process. Polymers used for electrospinning. Methods of estimating of nanofiber properties. Directions of application of nanofibers. Interactive nanofibers. Nanocoatings: Types and material used for coating and surface modification, application process, properties and uses. Nonotechnology in Textile Finishing: Methods, properties of obtained fibers and textile products, the latest achievements and directions of development. Highly advanced textile processing techniques applying nanotechnology such as Nano-Care, Nano-Pel, Nano-Dry, Nano-Tough, Nano-Press their characteristic and received effects.
